title.title: Special Kähler manifolds have virtually abelian $\pi_1$
title.subtitle: Claim: every special compact Kähler manifold has a virtually abelian fundamental group

plain: Shapes with no hidden 'general type' pieces have loops that behave almost like a simple grid of directions

beats.text: Special: no fibration onto an orbifold of general type (schematic)
Campana: no special manifold sits outside the virtually abelian set
So every compact Kähler manifold with $\kappa = 0$ would have virtually abelian $\pi_1$

achievement.label: Campana's abelianity conjecture (2004)
achievement.context: Before: known only for linear representations of $\pi_1$
achievement.note: Cites the release's own Shafarevich counterexample (family 046)

verify.detail: No Lean; the proof uses $L^2$ Dolbeault spectral analysis on the universal cover
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Campana's abelianity conjecture for special manifolds.
Special manifolds, in Campana's sense, have no fibration onto anything of general type.
Campana predicted their fundamental groups are virtually abelian.
Claimed: true for every special compact Kähler manifold.
